metaDescription: Five benchtop band saws under $300 compared on throat, resaw height, motor and speed, plus what a budget band saw gives up on blade tracking and resawing.
expertTake: The ShopMax 10-inch, with a 4.2-amp induction motor and 4.5 inches of cut height, is the best budget band saw for resawing and curves. The DeWalt 9-inch is the pick for two speeds, a worklight and a known service network, and the SKIL BW9501 is the quiet induction option. The WEN 9-inch is the lowest-risk entry, and the VEVOR is the pick if you want a cast table. Spend the first hour setting the blade, because a well-tuned cheap saw beats a badly tuned good one.
introParagraphs: A band saw is a long loop of toothed steel stretched over two wheels, cutting in one direction through a table. It cuts curves, resaws thick boards into thin ones and cuts odd shapes that a table saw cannot, and the key numbers are the throat, the height under the guides and the motor.
This guide explains how wheel size, blade width and motor type decide what a budget band saw can cut, which compromises a homeowner can accept and which turn the saw into a frustration.

products.name: SHOPMAX 4.2-Amp 10 in Benchtop Band Saw
products.description:
The ShopMax is the biggest of the budget band saws, with a 10-inch throat and 4.5 inches of cutting height. A 4.2-amp induction motor is quieter and smoother than a universal motor and is the main reason to choose this saw, since induction motors run at a steady speed and do not use carbon brushes. The table tilts 45 degrees.

The blade is a 67.4-inch loop, wider than the 59-1/2-inch blades on 9-inch saws, and the saw accepts widths from 0.14 to 0.47 inch. A wider blade holds a straight line better in resawing, and a narrow one turns tighter curves. The extra cut height lets you resaw a 4-inch board into two thinner boards, where the 9-inch saws top out at 3-1/2 inches.

Ownership is about setup. Adjust the tension, track the blade on the wheel and set the guides before the first cut. This is the pick for woodworkers who want a bit more capacity than the standard 9-inch size. Before buying blades, note the 67.4-inch length, because it is not the 59-1/2-inch blade that most benchtop saws use and fewer shops stock it. Order two spare blades with the saw, one wide for resawing and one narrow for curves.
products.bestFor: Woodworkers who want the largest throat and cut height at the cap.
pros: Induction motor is quiet and steady
Wide blade range from 0.14 to 0.47 in
cons: Larger blade size costs more to replace

products.name: DeWalt 9 in 3.5-Amp Two-Speed Band Saw with LED
products.description:
The DeWalt 9-inch band saw is a straightforward benchtop saw with a 3.5-amp motor and two blade speeds, listed as 1,700 and 2,500. The listing labels them strokes per minute, but on a band saw the figure is normally blade travel in feet per minute. The slow speed is for plastics and thin or delicate material, and the high speed is for wood. A band saw cuts cooler at the lower speed, which matters because plastic melts and welds itself shut behind a hot blade. An integrated LED lights the cut line.

Compared with the ShopMax 10-inch, the DeWalt has a smaller throat and a lower amp rating, but it carries a brand with service parts and blades widely stocked. A 9-inch saw cuts about 3-1/2 inches deep and 9 inches wide, which handles most small shop work. The 9 inches is the throat, the distance from the blade to the frame, so a 9-inch saw can cut to the middle of an 18-inch panel and no deeper.

Ownership comes down to blade setup and brand reputation. Check the tension and tracking before the first cut, set the upper guide close to the work and keep the blade sharp. For a woodworker who values warranty and parts over raw capacity, this is the safe pick.
products.bestFor: Hobbyists who want a known brand with two speeds and a work light.
pros: Two speeds for wood and plastics
cons: Smaller throat than the 10 in saw
Cut height limited to 9 in class

products.name: SKIL BW9501-00 2.8-Amp 9 in 2-Speed Band Saw
products.description:
The SKIL BW9501 uses a 2.8-amp induction motor, a 2-speed drive and a tool-free belt tensioning system. Induction motors are quieter than universal motors and hold a steady speed under load, which makes the saw a better fit for a garage where noise matters. A quick blade tension setting is meant to speed setup.

At 2.8 amps it has less motor current than the DeWalt's 3.5 and the ShopMax's 4.2. Induction amps are not directly comparable to universal amps, but in practice the SKIL is a light-duty saw for curves in thin stock and small resaws. The two speeds let you slow down for plastics and thin material.

Ownership details: setting tension by a quick gauge is a convenience, but a gauge on a cheap saw is only approximate, so use the flutter test, which is to tension the blade until it stops fluttering on a thin cut. Keep the wheels clean and the tires free of pitch. For a quiet, simple 9-inch saw it is a good value.
products.bestFor: People who want a quiet induction motor and a simple 9 in saw.

products.name: WEN BA3959 9 in 2.8-Amp Benchtop Band Saw
products.description:
The WEN BA3959 is the simple entry saw. A 2.8-amp motor turns the blade at up to 2,500 feet per minute, and it cuts up to 3-1/2 inches deep and 9 inches wide using a 59-1/2-inch blade between 1/8 and 3/8 inch. The blade length is standard for 9-inch saws, so replacements are easy to find.

Compared with the SKIL BW9501, the WEN has a single speed and a universal-style motor claim of 2.8 amps. Next to the ShopMax, it cuts a full inch shallower and 1 inch narrower. For curves in 3/4-inch boards and small resaws, the capacity is enough.

Ownership notes: a universal motor is louder than an induction motor, and the stock blade is a basic one. Tune the guides, set tension carefully and buy a better blade. It is the lowest-risk way to try a band saw. Learn the saw on scrap pine first: practice tensioning, tracking and straight cuts before you cut a good board, since a first resaw attempt on walnut is an expensive way to learn that the blade drifted. If you later want more capacity, the WEN's standard blade length means your spare blades will still fit other 9-inch saws.
products.bestFor: First-time band saw buyers who want a simple, widely stocked 9 in saw.
pros: Standard 59-1/2 in blade is easy to find
Cuts 3-1/2 in deep and 9 in wide

products.name: VEVOR 9 in 1/2 HP Benchtop Band Saw with Cast Table
products.description:
The VEVOR is a 9-inch benchtop saw with a half-horsepower, 373-watt motor and a cast table that measures 11.8 by 11.8 inches. The table tilts 5 degrees left and 45 degrees right, and a fence and miter gauge are included. It cuts to about 3.5 inches in height and uses a 60-inch blade.

A cast table is flatter and holds a miter gauge groove more accurately than a stamped sheet-metal table. Compared with the SKIL and WEN, the VEVOR's table is the strongest feature, and its blade length is 60 inches instead of the standard 59-1/2, so check blade stock before you buy a replacement.

Ownership is about alignment. Check that the table is square to the blade, set the fence parallel to the blade and pay attention to blade tracking. The fence and miter gauge give you straight rips and crosscuts, which is helpful when you are learning. Keep in mind that a band saw blade drifts, so a fixed fence can fight the cut: most woodworkers use a pivot point or a freehand line, and the fence works best once you have found the blade's natural drift angle on scrap.
products.bestFor: Woodworkers who want a flat cast table and included fence at a low cost.
pros: Cast table is flat and stable
cons: 60 in blade is a less common length

buyingCriteria.explanation: The throat is the distance from blade to frame, and the resaw height is the clearance under the guides. A 9-inch saw cuts about 3-1/2 inches deep, and the ShopMax 10-inch cuts 4.5. Resaw height decides how thick a board you can split. If you want to make thin veneers or book-matched panels, only the ShopMax gets close to 5 inches. Do not buy a 9-inch saw if you plan to resaw 4-inch stock.

Induction motors are quieter and hold speed without brushes. The ShopMax and SKIL BW9501 use induction motors. Universal motors, which are in many cheaper saws, are louder and wear brushes. For a garage or apartment, induction is worth having.

Blade length is model-specific. 9-inch saws like the WEN use 59-1/2-inch blades, the ShopMax uses 67.4 inches and the VEVOR uses 60. A saw that uses a common length is cheaper to run. Blade width decides what curves you can cut.

Blade tracking and tension decide cut quality more than motor size. A saw with a good tensioning knob and wheel alignment makes setup easier. Cheap saws often need fiddling to track true. A quick test is to spin the wheel by hand and watch whether the blade stays centered on the tire; if it creeps toward an edge, the saw needs adjustment before it cuts anything.
A flat table, a miter slot that fits a gauge and a tilt scale that is accurate are signs of a good saw. The VEVOR's cast table is flatter than a stamped one.
Two speeds, like the DeWalt's 1,700 and 2,500, let you slow down for plastics and thin material. A single-speed saw is fine for wood only.

specDecoder.meaning: The distance from the blade to the saw frame, which sets the widest cut. The ShopMax is 10 inches and the others 9.
specDecoder.watchFor: A bigger throat does not give more cutting height.

specDecoder.meaning: The clearance between the table and the upper guide. The ShopMax lists 4.5 inches.
specDecoder.watchFor: Cut height shrinks if the guide is not raised fully.

specDecoder.meaning: The blade speed. The DeWalt runs at 1,700 or 2,500.
specDecoder.watchFor: Slow speed is for plastic and thin material.

specDecoder.meaning: A brushless AC motor that runs smoother and quieter than a universal motor.
specDecoder.watchFor: Its amps do not compare directly with universal amps.

specDecoder.meaning: How the blade sits on the wheel tires. It decides whether the blade stays centered.
specDecoder.watchFor: Poor tracking makes the blade wander in the cut.

cards.label: 9 inch
cards.text: Cuts about 3-1/2 inches deep and uses a common 59-1/2 in blade. The WEN, SKIL, DeWalt and VEVOR fit here.

cards.label: 10 inch
cards.text: Cuts 4.5 inches deep and 10 inches wide. The ShopMax fits here.

howToChoose.note: Choose 9 inches for general work and 10 for resaw.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: At least 4 inches of height, a wide blade and a stable induction motor. Tension firmly and feed slowly.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The ShopMax is the only saw with 4.5 inches of height. The 9-inch saws top out at 3-1/2.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You resaw hardwood weekly or need a 14-inch saw. A bigger saw has more power and capacity.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cut curves in thin stock. The WEN or SKIL is enough.

maintenance.why: Wrong tension makes the blade wander. Too little tension lets the blade bow in a thick cut, and too much stresses the frame and shortens blade life. Use the gauge as a start, then fine-tune by listening and watching the cut.
Pitch buildup makes the blade track poorly.

Guides stop the blade from twisting. Set them about the thickness of a piece of paper from the blade and lower the upper guide to just above the work, which also keeps your fingers farther from the teeth.
A dull blade burns and drifts.

faq.q: What can a band saw do that a jigsaw cannot?
faq.a: A band saw cuts thick stock in a straight line or a smooth curve, and it can resaw a board into thinner boards. A jigsaw cannot do that.
For curves and small resaws, yes. For 4-inch resaw, choose a 10-inch.

faq.q: Do I need an induction motor?
faq.a: Not essential, but it is quieter and steadier.
A 1/4 inch, 6 teeth per inch blade is a good start. A wider blade, about 1/2 inch, for resaw, and a 1/8 inch blade only for tight curves.
Poor tracking, a dull blade or a wrong guide setup. Adjust and sharpen.
Only with a metal-cutting saw. A wood band saw cuts thin aluminum on a slow speed.
